newsitem.title: INDONESIA: About 150 Megawati supporters gather in Jakarta.
newsitem.headline: About 150 Megawati supporters gather in Jakarta.

text.p: About 150 supporters of Indonesia's ousted minority party leader Megawati Sukarnoputri gathered outside parliament on Thursday at the start of a protest demonstration.

The demonstrators had said they planned to meet the speaker of parliament and march to Jakarta police headquarters to protest against lack of action against the man who ousted Megawati as leader of the Indonesian Democratic Party (PDI).
Demonstrators were gathering in the parking lot of the parliament complex after 10 a.m. (0300 GMT). Organisers had said they hoped for about 2,000 to 3,000 people by around 11 a.m.
"Our plan is to meet with the Speaker of parliament to have a dialogue," one participant told Reuters.
There was no extra security evident other than the usual guards at parliament.
There was no immediate indication whether the march or motorcade to police headquarters, adjacent to the stock exchange building in central Jakarta, would go ahead.

The demonstrators are complaining that the authorities targeted Megawati supporters for arrest following a July 27 assault on the PDI headquarters by backers of Megawati's rival, Surjadi, the deputy speaker of parliament.
The attack sparked the worst rioting in Jakarta in more than two decades in which five people died.
Last month. 115 Megawati loyalists charged with disobeying police orders and refusing to disperse in the July 27 incident were released after serving four months in jail. Nine others were acquitted.

The official National Commission on Human Rights in a report on the July 27 events criticised the government for arresting only Megawati supporters, while members of the government-backed Surjadi faction were not detained.
Megawati, daughter of Indondesia's founding president Sukarno, was ousted as leader of the PDI by Surjadi at a government-financed rebel congress in June.
Political analysts said the government was concerned that she might draw votes away from the ruling Golkar party in general elections next May.
